question: Should OpenClaw adopt this durable AI-safety event store, operator query surface, and public plugin emission API as a permanent core contract, and if so what privacy, retention, and external-plugin permissions apply?
rationale: The proposed behavior creates new durable telemetry, operator access, Gateway methods, and a plugin SDK/manifest capability. Those are product and compatibility choices, not a mechanically derivable bug fix.

options.title: Approve a narrowed core contract
options.body: Define the allowed event fields, retention, access controls, and plugin permission semantics, then reduce the PR to that approved contract and prove it end to end.

options.title: Keep only an internal diagnostics seam
options.body: Avoid a public plugin API and durable operator UI until maintainers have separately designed the external contract.

options.title: Route optional observability integrations outward
options.body: Keep core diagnostics generic and move specialized dashboards or exporter behavior to plugins once a minimal supported seam exists.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrowed core contract
recommendation.body: Define the allowed event fields, retention, access controls, and plugin permission semantics, then reduce the PR to that approved contract and prove it end to end.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal and implementation history make skoya the best available routing contact from the supplied evidence, though final product acceptance requires a repository decision-maker.
